rationale: C polymon calls instapetrify after losing stone resistance while riding a touch-petrifying steed and rnl(3) succeeds. The corresponding JS branch prints the warning then note_unported, omitting the fatal/petrification operation. This is an explicit semantic omission; supported full-game construction and actual reachability have not been validated.
JS executes docrt for the production singleton state. The stub is only the alternate injected-state branch. A lexical stub anywhere in the owner does not prove production omission.

For the evaluated standard recorder configuration, debug_fuzzer is not enabled. C and JS guard fuzzer_savelife at done with that flag. This classification is scoped to ordinary recorder inputs, not a proof for every possible debug build; the source omission remains relevant if that configuration is later supported.

JS awaits the implemented quest_chat and records a stub only if it returns failure for an impossible unknown character. The call edge and regular quest path exist. Do not count this defensive marker as wholesale missing quest chat.

C emits a bounds diagnostic when bubble.x+mask exceeds xmax; JS clamps the same bound without the print. Whether a supported game can reach the abnormal bound is unproven. Keep this and the C-only pline edge as one investigation group; no gameplay defect claim.

The C final is_db_wall branch emits a visible-monster disappearance message (and related hero portcullis text). The corresponding JS branch immediately tests survival/death and returns with no visible message branch. This is source-confirmed omitted behavior, independent of exact string construction; no C recording or root-cause novelty claim yet.

Same bounded-bubble diagnostic omission as the selected message lead. Both IDs are retained but linked to one candidate cause; valid runtime reachability of the out-of-bounds correction is not established.

C monst_to_any packages the monster pointer for the light API. JS passes state.youmonst directly to its object-valued light API. Both old-light deletion and new-light creation are present; no omitted light transition is established by the wrapper edge.
The reverse JS on_level edge implements C Is_airlevel/Is_waterlevel macro checks. It is a macro-to-function representation change, not an extra gameplay operation.
C ACURR(A_CON) expands to acurr(x); JS calls acurr(state,A_CON). The reverse edge is a header macro expansion, not extra behavior.

The literal C call is absent in JS, but the main workflow established that supported gameplay cannot reach the relevant mounted-petrifying-steed state: saddle rules exclude cockatrices/chickatrices, and polymorphing a mounted steed into them dismounts first. The reported controlled pony-to-cockatrice replay matched 2866 RNG entries and 129 screens plus cursors. Supersedes the earlier semantic-omission classification; no supported gameplay defect is established.
